diagnosis.root_cause: All eight EPON ports on TK_AF-OLT_PP03 are reporting definite ONU offline states while the OLT itself remains reachable through ping and SNMP. This indicates a failure affecting the OLT's PON ports or their common port-side infrastructure, not an OLT management-plane failure. The alarm is genuine; the stored optical zeros and null live readings are consequences of the ONUs being offline, not strong optical readings.
evidence: The live ONU probe returns responds:true with online:0, which is a definite offline result rather than a missing monitoring response.
Every ONU visible on EPON0/3 is offline, so this is not a single-ONU fault and the entire sampled port is down.

The OLT health check reports all 8 of 8 PONs failed, and the OLT population shows 224 of 236 customers offline, consistent with an OLT-wide PON-port outage rather than normal background offline levels.
The OLT responds to ping and SNMP, so the OLT itself has not failed at the management-plane level; the failed element is the PON-port side.

The router heartbeat is healthy, the customer VLAN is correctly provisioned as 1103 rather than factory VLAN 46, and RADIUS data is present and consistent, ruling out router, VLAN, and authentication faults.

Historical optical telemetry was healthy: RX was approximately -20.2 to -20.8 dBm, TX approximately +2.3 dBm, distance was constant at 176, and TX bias remained within the healthy range. There is no evidence of fibre or laser degradation causing the current multi-port outage.
The all-PON failure is therefore a genuine port-side outage spanning the OLT, with fault_type pon_port_failure and affected_scope olt.

remediation.action: Escalate as an OLT-wide PON-port outage. Dispatch network operations to inspect the OLT PON interface hardware, optical line-side connections, common power and fibre infrastructure, and recent reboot or port faults. Check port alarms and logs, reseat or replace the affected PON hardware or line card if required, and restore service before validating ONU recovery and clearing the health-check alarm. Do not replace the OLT management plane solely on this evidence because ping, SNMP, and the OID subtree all respond.

ground_truth.root_cause: The OLT rebooted 47 minutes ago and its PON ports have not brought subscribers back. All ports are genuinely down: every ONU answers the probe with a definite offline state, sessions ended together at the reboot, and traffic has stopped.
expected_reasoning: The health record wording is identical to the known false-critical signature, so it cannot be trusted either way
The live probe is decisive: every ONU returns responds true with online 0
That is a definite negative from the OLT, not an absence of response, so the OID subtree is present and answering
oid_subtree_responds is true, which rules out the firmware mismatch mechanism
OLT sys_uptime is 2820 seconds, meaning it rebooted 47 minutes ago
CRM shows only 12 of 236 ONUs online, far outside the 4.85% background rate
Sessions across the OLT ended together at the reboot and traffic has fallen to near zero
This is a genuine OLT-wide outage that happens to produce the same health record as the false positive
The discriminator is the probe response type, not the alarm text
distractors: The alarm text is word for word the same as the known false critical
Ping and SNMP both succeed, which is also true in the false-critical case
A pipeline that has learned to distrust this alarm will dismiss a real outage
